thread:
Sylvia: Heads-up — ran a perf sweep on the hybrid 4-bit + FP8 stack in staging. p50 is fine but p99 for long windows (>=8k tokens) jumped ~12-18% when the continuous-batcher merges variable-length requests into the stripe-256 bucket.
Rahul: Can you paste the exact shape-bucketing config you used? Did you repro with kvcache warm vs cold? :thinking_face:
Sylvia: Repro steps below and the bucket config. kvcache warm shows the same regression (so not a cold-cache miss spike).
```
continuous_batcher:
  shape_bucketing:
    thresholds: [64, 128, 256, 512]
    merge_bias: prefer_smaller
    max_merge_stride: 512
kernel_selector:
  quant_priority: speed
  tie_break: prefer_quantized
```
Sylvia: Notice the regression only when stride patterns are uneven (e.g., requests with long prefix then many short tails). I suspect the hybrid4fp8 kernels pick the 4-bit path for some shapes, which triggers extra packing memcpy on our slab allocator when stride%64 != 0.
Marco: Pulled telemetry: https://console.redwood.ai/perf/series/abcd — see p99 delta between hybrid vs fp8-only. Also added a quick flamegraph for the hot path: `kernel_pack -> pack_memcpy -> kv_slab_realign`.
eden-bot: deploy/status staging-hybrid4fp8: completed 2026-03-18T12:03:15Z (no infra alerts).
Rahul: If packing memcpy is the culprit we should try two experiments: (1) avoid merging shapes with stride > 128 into the same bucket, (2) prefer FP8 float path when stride misalignment detected. The first reduces pack work, second avoids quant kernel that forces packing.
Sylvia: Will run experiment-1 now (shape threshold tweak) with this command: `./run_perf --suite=hybrid4fp8 --nodes=2 --workload=continuous-batch --tag=exp-shape-threshold`
Marco: FYI the change will increase padding waste for the small shapes because we won't merge them as aggressively. Need to track pad_waste_ratio metric.
Rahul: Good point. Add pad_waste_ratio and kv_realign_count to perf dashboard. Also add a kernel_selector telemetry tag that records why a kernel was chosen (tie-break reason).
Sylvia: Quick back-of-envelope after experiment-1: p99 improved by ~9% vs the original hybrid run, p50 unchanged, pad_waste_ratio went from 0.07 -> 0.14 (so ~2x). kv_realign_count dropped ~70%.
Marco: That's promising — trade looks acceptable for latency-sensitive SLAs. For throughput SLOs we might lose cost efficiency. Let's run experiment-2: prefer FP8 path on odd strides and measure.
Rahul: Also open a small runtime PR to add a kernel_selector override flag `prefer_no_realign` so SRE/product can toggle without redeploying kernels.
Sylvia: I'll open the PR and attach perf run results. Action items: (1) Sylvia — PR + exp-2 perf run, (2) Marco — dashboard tiles for pad_waste_ratio & kernel_tiebreak, (3) Rahul — spec for prefer_no_realign toggle + notes for rollout.
Marco: tagging this thread in the daily standup notes. :white_check_mark:
Sylvia: Thanks — I'll post the perf logs and a short replay gist when exp-2 finishes.
